references.text: Abraham emphasizes the importance of choosing a wife from his own people, in contrast to Esau, who took Hittite women.
Rebekah complains about Esau's Hittite wives, indicating the family's dissatisfaction with his choices.
Esau realizes that his Canaanite wives are not accepted by his parents, so he takes a wife from Ishmael's descendants in an attempt to make amends.
Details about Esau's wives, including the Hittites, and their families, showing his integration with local tribes.
Complementary accounts illustrating Esau's repeated poor choices in marriage and his failure to separate himself from the people.
Text-critical correlation revealing name variations (Basemath/Ada) and confirming Esau's systematic choice of Canaanite wives.
Genealogical link confirming that the wife mentioned in Gen 26:34 is the mother of one of Esau's clan founders.
Confirmation of the fertility of the wives mentioned in Gen 26:34.
Complementary account showing that Esau also took a Hivite wife (Oholibamah) alongside the Hittites.
Genealogical confirmation that the wife Basemath from Gen 26:34 is the mother of Reuel's clan.
